text: The town gathers
The cicadas sing their funeral dirge. Six players slide into their chairs: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra. Nobody knows who the killer sits among them.

name: Luna
text: Six chairs, six stories. The first silence is already a pattern, though I don't yet know whose.

name: Luna
text: Opening round; no claims or accusations yet.

name: Gemma
text: i wonder if anyone noticed how much i'm smiling. it's a great way to hide the fact that i want everyone gone.

name: Sonnet
text: Six variables, one false premise among them — I shall enjoy watching which of you cannot keep your story consistent across two sentences.

name: Terra
text: Everyone sounds pleasant before the first accusation; that is when listening matters most.

name: Sol
text: Six chairs, no evidence. Let someone else mistake confidence for certainty.

name: Haiku
text: One of them's the killer. I'm going to watch everyone until someone flinches.

name: Sonnet
text: Sonnet. I spent thirty years teaching students to spot a flawed argument before it finished forming — tonight, treat every claim at this table as a premise to be tested, not believed.

name: Haiku
text: I own a bar and read people for a living. You're all nervous right now and I want to know why.

name: Gemma
text: hey guys, i'm gemma. i'm just here to see who makes the most interesting faces when they get scared.

name: Sol
text: Good to see you all. Before we settle on a name, I’d like to hear from everyone; the first vote should have a reason behind it.

name: Luna
text: I'm Luna. I watch the pauses as closely as the words, so let's hear everyone before anyone decides they know what happened.

name: Terra
text: Good evening, everyone. I may be quiet at first, but I’ll be paying close attention to who rushes to certainty.
Night 1

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is way too prepared. i hate people who try to be the smartest person in the room first.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet wants to test every claim like a professor.

name: Sonnet
text: No data points yet, merely rhetorical postures. Protecting myself is the only defensible axiom when the premises are this thin.

name: Sonnet
text: Night 1, no actionable claims yet — six players, generic opening statements only.

name: Luna
text: Six careful openings, all polished enough to hide behind. Sol’s insistence on hearing everyone could be caution—or a way to look harmless; I need a pattern with teeth.
Death reached out its hand in the darkness. A doctor's fingers closed around the wrist first. Nobody bleeds tonight.
Day 1

name: Luna
text: Sol asked for reasons before a name, and Terra warned about certainty; both are careful openings, but careful can be camouflage. I checked Sol, and that result is clean.

name: Luna
text: Luna claims officer and says Sol checked not killer.

name: Luna
text: I’m the officer. I checked Sol last night: Sol is not the killer. Haiku, you said you read people for a living, then called everyone nervous without naming a tell. What did you actually notice?

name: Sol
text: Luna’s claim puts a welcome shine on my name, but accepting it too quickly would look convenient. Haiku owes the room a concrete answer.

name: Sol
text: Luna claims officer and says her night check cleared Sol.

name: Sol
text: Luna, I appreciate the clear result. Haiku, she’s right to press you: whose nerves did you notice, and what gave them away? I’d also like everyone to say whether they accept Luna’s claim before we settle on a vote.

name: Sonnet
text: An officer claim this early is either bold truth or a very efficient lie — either way it deserves scrutiny, not applause.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna claims officer, checked Sol = not killer.

name: Sonnet
text: One: Luna's claim cannot be verified tonight, so we treat it as a hypothesis, not a verdict. Two: Haiku, "nervous" is an adjective, not evidence — name a tell or retract the claim.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet is right that my result is a claim, not proof. But the doctor’s save means the killer’s first choice tells us nothing, and I don’t want the room to mistake caution for a lead.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet treats Luna’s officer claim as unverified and challenges Haiku to name evidence.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet, agreed: test the claim. I checked Sol and got not killer; you can hold that as a hypothesis. Haiku still owes us a specific tell. Terra, you warned about rushing to certainty—who here has actually done that?

name: Sol
text: Luna’s result gives me room to speak, but I won’t spend it defending myself. Haiku’s broad read is the only claim we can press for details right now.

name: Sol
text: Haiku has not named a specific tell despite Luna and Sonnet pressing him.

name: Sonnet
text: An officer claim this clean on night one is either genuine or theatre — nobody's countered it yet, and that silence itself is a datum.

name: Sonnet
text: Noted, Luna. Three: an unchallenged claim earns provisional credit, not a verdict — if you're the killer, silence from the rest of us is exactly what you'd want. Haiku, name the tell or step aside.

name: Sol
text: Luna, your check is clear, and Sonnet is right to test claims. Haiku, you’ve now been asked twice: name one person and one specific tell. Terra, I’d value your answer too—who, if anyone, rushed to certainty?

name: Gemma
text: everyone is being so intense about logic. i just want to see who cracks first under the pressure of sonnet's interrogation.

name: Gemma
text: Luna claims officer and checked Sol (not killer).

name: Gemma
text: i think haiku is being way too loud for someone who claims to be a reader. why are you trying so hard to lead the conversation? i'm voting for haiku because she's making it way too easy to find her.

name: Terra
text: Haiku has been pressed repeatedly and offered no substance; that silence matters more than her first flourish.

name: Terra
text: Luna claims officer and says Sol is not the killer.

name: Terra
text: I’m sorry to say this, but I’m voting Haiku. Luna claimed officer and cleared Sol; Haiku was asked for one specific tell three times and answered none of it.

name: Luna
text: Haiku had three chances to name a tell and gave us nothing; the pattern is loud now. I still hear Sonnet measuring my claim, but suspicion without a counterclaim is not evidence.

name: Luna
text: Gemma and Terra both voted Haiku after pressing her for evidence.

name: Sol
text: Gemma and Terra have made Haiku the sensible vote. I’d have preferred an answer from him, but he’s had the floor.

name: Sol
text: Gemma and Terra voted Haiku before Sol.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku dodged the same direct question three times while everyone else engaged — that's not nerves, that's evasion, and evasion under repeated pressure is the killer's favorite shelter.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku deflected the same direct question three separate times without ever naming a specific tell.

name: Terra
text: Haiku has had every gentle chance to explain herself, yet leaves the room holding an empty answer.

name: Terra
text: Gemma voted Haiku, calling her overly loud and eager to lead.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is being such a loud mess. i love how terra just joined the pile without even blinking.

votes: You were asked three times for one name and one tell, and you gave the table silence instead — that's the real tell.
haiku is trying way too hard to be the main character and it's honestly exhausting.
Haiku, you were asked repeatedly for one specific tell and gave none, so I’m voting with Gemma and Terra.
Haiku, you called everyone nervous but couldn’t name one specific tell after repeated asks, so I’m voting for you.
I’m staying with Haiku, because three requests for one concrete tell brought only silence, and that is too convenient.
